stories.body: Nearly 130 heads of state and government are expected in New York as the UN General Assembly's high-level debate begins, dominated by the wars in the Middle East and Ukraine, climate and economic pressures, and growing concern about artificial intelligence. Secretary-General António Guterres is expected to deliver his final annual address, while Brazil will speak first and US President Donald Trump is scheduled to follow. The gathering comes as the UN faces a liquidity and credibility crisis and leaders warn that multilateral institutions are weakening; Palestinian President Mahmoud Abbas is again expected to address the assembly remotely after the US denied visas to Palestinian officials.
stories.headline: World leaders gather for the UN General Assembly amid wars, AI concerns and deepening global divisions

stories.body: Houthi forces are battling Saudi-backed Yemeni government troops for the strategically important Kahboub Mountains after extending their control along Yemen's Red Sea coast, including the port of Mokha. Control of the heights overlooking the Bab al-Mandab strait and Mayyun Island could cut the coast off from government-held southern territory. Saudi strikes on Mokha reportedly killed at least six people, while the renewed fighting has killed hundreds and displaced more than 125,000 people since early September. US media reported that Donald Trump called off planned US strikes on the Houthis at the last minute despite Saudi appeals for intervention, underscoring Washington's reluctance to open another military commitment in the region.
stories.headline: Fighting in Yemen escalates as Houthis seize strategic ground and Saudi strikes hit Mokha

stories.body: Typhoon Dujuan has killed at least four people in landslides near Tokyo, injured 22 and left tens of thousands of homes without power as it moved away from Japan. At the height of the storm, authorities urged more than 1.6 million people across the Tokyo region to evacuate, warning of an imminent threat to life. The typhoon brought violent winds and record rainfall, including 832mm over 48 hours on Oshima island, disrupted hundreds of flights and forced the cancellation or early closure of major events. Officials have downgraded many warnings, but rescuers continue searching for missing people in affected areas.
stories.headline: Typhoon Dujuan kills at least four in Japan as evacuations are ordered for millions

stories.body: Russian missile and drone attacks killed three people in Dnipro, wounded six and damaged industrial sites and energy infrastructure across Ukraine, officials said. A strike on a power facility in Chernihiv left nearly 100,000 consumers without electricity, while Ukraine said the overnight barrage involved 212 drones and several missiles. Ukraine also struck Russia's Samara region with drones, killing one person, according to the regional governor. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has arrived in New York for the UN General Assembly, where he says he plans about 20 meetings, including a likely meeting with Donald Trump, and hopes to sign a drone agreement to strengthen Ukrainian air defence and financing.
stories.headline: Russian strikes kill three in Ukraine as Zelenskyy arrives in the US for the UN summit

stories.body: Major US television networks have suspended pooled coverage of Donald Trump's events after CNN, Politico and MS NOW were barred from the White House. The administration accused the outlets of publishing fiction or lies, while the affected organizations said they would sue, arguing that revoking journalists' credentials over reporting violates the First Amendment. Other outlets, including The New York Times and The Washington Post, also declined to share material from pooled events, leaving no network television footage of Trump's trip to New York for the UN General Assembly. The White House subsequently launched a 24-hour streaming channel, Trump TV.
stories.headline: Major US media outlets boycott Trump events after the White House bans several news organizations

stories.body: British Columbia has sued OpenAI and its chief executive, Sam Altman, in a California federal court, alleging that the company failed to alert police after its safety team identified ChatGPT conversations in which the Tumbler Ridge school shooter discussed gun violence. The province says the February attack, which killed eight people including six children, might have been prevented and seeks damages for recovery and rebuilding costs as well as changes to OpenAI's handling of conversations indicating a risk of violence. OpenAI has expressed sympathy and said it remains committed to working with government and law-enforcement authorities, while families affected by the shooting have filed separate cases.
stories.headline: British Columbia sues OpenAI and Sam Altman over the Tumbler Ridge school shooting

stories.body: Republicans are spending heavily to defend House and Senate seats in states and districts Donald Trump won comfortably in 2024 as concerns over tariffs, diesel prices and broader affordability weigh on voter sentiment. Since August, more than $110 million in Republican advertising has gone to districts Trump carried by double digits, while party leaders are trying to shore up races in Ohio, Iowa, Kansas, Alaska and Texas. GOP operatives say Trump's approval is underwater in some deeply Republican states, and candidates are increasingly pressing for relief from high fuel costs and an end to the Iran war. Republicans retain a significant financial advantage and structural benefits in the Senate map, but party officials privately describe an expanding defensive battlefield.
stories.headline: Republicans expand their midterm defense as economic and tariff concerns put deep-red seats at risk

stories.body: Immigrants with final deportation orders are no longer appearing in Immigration and Customs Enforcement's online detainee locator, a change that makes it harder for families and attorneys to determine where people are being held after they enter ICE custody.
stories.headline: Immigrants with final deportation orders disappear from ICE's detainee locator

stories.body: Hundreds of flights were delayed and ground stops were imposed at major airports in New York, New Jersey, Pennsylvania and Massachusetts after construction workers severed a telecommunications cable used by air traffic control. Newark was the most heavily affected, with hundreds of arriving and departing flights delayed, while JFK, LaGuardia and Philadelphia also faced disruption. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said the cable was repaired and operations would resume, though delays were expected to continue. The outage came immediately before the UN General Assembly, when numerous world leaders were due to arrive in the New York area.
stories.headline: Technical problems halt or delay flights at major Northeast US airports

stories.body: New York Governor Kathy Hochul says she is considering additional AI safeguards as the state's RAISE Act approaches its January effective date, including whether a kill-switch requirement for the most advanced AI models would be feasible and serve the public interest. Hochul stressed that she was not committing to the proposal and said research would guide the state's decisions. Her comments follow a California executive order exploring a similar requirement, while some technology companies argue that such a mechanism is not technically practical and federal legislation remains stalled.
stories.headline: New York Governor Kathy Hochul considers further AI safeguards, including a possible kill-switch requirement

stories.body: Judge Juan Carlos Peinado has ordered Begoña Gómez, the wife of Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez, to stand trial before a popular jury on allegations of influence peddling and embezzlement; her former Moncloa adviser Cristina Álvarez faces an embezzlement charge. The case began nearly two and a half years ago with a complaint by the far-right-linked group Manos Limpias and has drawn repeated criticism of the investigation. Madrid's provincial court will set the trial date, which could take several months. Gómez, Álvarez and the public prosecutor's office seek acquittal, while the government says the investigation has been politically motivated.
stories.headline: Judge sends Begoña Gómez, the Spanish prime minister's wife, to trial by jury over alleged influence peddling and embezzlement

stories.body: Spain's foreign minister, José Manuel Albares, says Madrid is coordinating with Moroccan authorities to deter a possible new mass crossing into Ceuta after calls circulated online for people to attempt one during Morocco's legislative elections. Albares said the messages did not appear to be gaining much traction, but Spain had activated preventive channels and a public-information campaign warning that irregular entry into Ceuta or Melilla does not confer a right to remain in Spain or travel freely through Europe. The response follows a July mass crossing in which official estimates of the number of arrivals and people remaining in Ceuta have varied sharply between central and local authorities.
stories.headline: Spain says Morocco is cooperating to prevent another mass crossing into Ceuta

stories.body: Spain is again pressing EU partners to grant official EU-language status to Catalan, Basque and Galician, with the government signaling that it could withhold approval for future enlargement if the issue remains unresolved. The matter is being raised at the EU General Affairs Council but is not expected to come to a vote. Sweden and Germany have warned that accession negotiations for countries such as Montenegro, Albania and Ukraine should not be tied to the language question, while several governments remain opposed to the proposal. Spain argues that millions of citizens who use co-official languages are being treated unequally within the Union.
stories.headline: Spain presses EU partners to make Catalan an official EU language and links the issue to enlargement

stories.body: Spain's Constitutional Court is beginning deliberations on the first appeal seeking the effective application of the amnesty law to Catalan independence leaders, starting with former minister and Junts secretary-general Jordi Turull's challenge over the embezzlement charge. The Supreme Court has refused to apply the amnesty to embezzlement, arguing that spending public money on the 2017 independence referendum constituted indirect enrichment and falls within the law's exceptions. A conservative Constitutional Court judge has backed that position in a draft ruling, but the court's progressive majority is expected to reject it and appoint a new rapporteur. Its eventual doctrine could also shape the prospects for former Catalan president Carles Puigdemont's return to Spain.
stories.headline: Spain's Constitutional Court begins deliberations on applying the amnesty law to Catalan independence leaders

stories.body: Barcelona's TMB bus drivers are holding a seven-hour stoppage from 10:00 to 17:00 to attend an extraordinary assembly after 23 unsuccessful meetings over their new collective agreement. Minimum service is set at 20% until 16:00 and 40% during the final hour, meaning substantially longer waits across all TMB bus routes. The Metro, Tram, Ferrocarrils de la Generalitat and Rodalies are not part of the action. Workers cite stalled talks over pay, a 35-hour workweek, schedules and legally required rest periods, and will decide whether to begin a broader period of mobilization.
stories.headline: Barcelona bus drivers begin a seven-hour strike, cutting service across the TMB network

stories.body: Barcelona has given initial approval to a gradual increase in the municipal tourist surcharge for cruise passengers who stop in the city for fewer than 12 hours, lifting it from €5 to €12 next year and eventually to €24 by 2030. The proposal passed with support from the PSC, ERC and Junts, while Barcelona en Comú opposed the slower timetable and the PP and Vox also voted against it. The city expects the change to more than double revenue from short-stay cruise visitors in 2027, with part of the additional income earmarked for free academic support and extracurricular activities for students. The tax ordinance still requires further votes before taking effect.
stories.headline: Barcelona moves toward raising its tourist surcharge on cruise-ship stopovers

stories.body: Pimec Comerç, the small-business association, has urged Barcelona to incorporate existing neighborhood shops, markets, small businesses, cooperatives and self-employed traders into the city's proposed affordable-food network rather than create a parallel publicly supported system. The city plans to test its first affordable supermarket in 2027 in the Marina del Prat Vermell, using a municipally owned space managed by a social-sector organization. Pimec supports making essential products more accessible but says the city should first assess local commercial supply, support established businesses with fair rules and address the production, transport, energy and labor costs that influence food prices.
stories.headline: Barcelona's small-business association urges the city to use existing local shops in its proposed affordable supermarket network

stories.body: The Mossos d'Esquadra are investigating the alleged forced abduction of a man in Barcelona's Sant Martí district after witnesses said several hooded people forced him into a vehicle early Monday. The man was found hours later near a petrol station in the Girona area, and investigators have made no arrests. Police have not established a financial demand and therefore have not formally characterized the case as kidnapping. It is not currently linked to a separate incident two days earlier on the AP-7 near Montornès del Vallès, where men posing as police forced another man from a car and later released him; officials say early indications in that case may point to drug-related activity.
stories.headline: Police investigate a second alleged express kidnapping in Catalunya in less than 48 hours
